newsitem.title: POLAND: ABN-AMRO rates Polish brewer Zywiec a sell.
newsitem.headline: ABN-AMRO rates Polish brewer Zywiec a sell.

text.p: ABN-Amro Hoare Govett recommended selling brewer Zaklady Piwowarskie w Zywcu SA (Zywiec) shares and said they were too expensive trading at about 50 times 1996 earnings.
Such a multiple put Zywiec at a premium of almost 400 percent to the Polish market, ABN-Amro Hoare Govett said in a report dated October 1 and released on Tuesday.

"The company is (also) valued at $118 per hectolitre making it the most expensive brewer in central Europe. We feel that these premiums are not justified and that the shares are due for a correction," ABN-Amro said.
Based on current earnings Zywiec's price-earnings ratio is at 27.4 versus 15 for the overall main market. The stock closed at 165.5 zlotys on October 1 and has since fallen to 159 zlotys.
ABN-Amro said increased beer demand in Poland would likely help lift Zywiec's production by 40 percent from last year to 2.1 million hectolitres in 1998.

But it said net income would fall 63 percent this year because of marketing expenses, a real-term drop in prices and investments that have lifted annual production capacity to 2.5 million hectolitres.
"Although we forecast an improvement (in net income), as of next year, the growth rate in real terms is likely to slow down," the report said.
ABN-Amro saw Zywiec's net income at 10 million zlotys this year, 13.5 million next year and 16.5 million in 1998 after the 27.1 million net income of last year.
